correctness.rationale: The published finite-graph contour theorem identifies asymptotic CCA rate with the largest unsigned directed simple-cycle color-difference mean. The identity delta_C=3delta_G+phi(endpoint)-phi(start), phi=(0,-2,-1), telescopes, proving same-initial-state rate factor three. For two adjacent missing hub spokes, fundamental cycles are n-3 surviving triangles plus one length-five cycle. Any rainbow triangle gives maximal rate 1; otherwise all cycle integrals are 0 or the five-cycle integral ±3, so the only intermediate rate is 3/5. A 3x3 nonrainbow transfer M and endpoint-pair winding matrix N yield R_mid=3tr(M^(n-3)N), recurrence t_(j+3)=3t_(j+2)-t_(j+1)-t_j and the remaining R0, R1 formulas. Checked n=6 population (729,378,1080), sum=2187=3^7. For nonadjacent deleted spokes, two length-four fundamental cycles produce rates 0,3/4 or (if equal nonzero circulation signs) 1 on the six-cycle, yielding the claimed placement contrast. Bounds hold for all n>=5 adjacent, n>=6 separated by graph structure, not finite test extrapolation.

value.rationale: For excitable deterministic networks, asymptotic firing rates and their initial-state populations are direct natural invariants. The exact split 0,3/5,1 for adjacent missing spokes, versus 0,3/4,1 for nonadjacent gaps on same-degree-sequence graphs, is a structural counterexample to degree-based rate determination. The nontrivial all-n transfer recurrence and conditional positive middle-phase fraction quantify the effect and may guide network-specific activity analysis; this is an independent exact result beyond general circulation theory.
